title: Injectives and the Cech acyclicity criterion
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small relative to a universe in which its hom-sets, coefficients and covering index sets lie, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings on it. Module sheaves mean sheaves of left $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; injectivity is in that category [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a basis of objects closed under the iterated fibre products of its covering families: for a covering $\{V_a\to U\}$ with $U,V_a\in\mathcal B$, all $V_{a_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U V_{a_p}$ lie in $\mathcal B$. Suppose every covering of an object $U\in\mathcal B$ admits a finite covering refinement $\{V_a\to U\}_{a=1}^m$ with $V_a\in\mathcal B$. For such a covering write $\check H^p(\mathcal V,M)$ for the cohomology of the alternating restriction complex of the underlying abelian presheaf of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], using all ordered tuples including repetitions. Then every injective module sheaf $I$ has $\check H^p(\mathcal V,I)=0$ for $p>0$ and every finite basis covering. If a module sheaf $M$ has this same vanishing for every finite basis covering, then $H^q(U,M)=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and $q>0$. Here $H^q(U,M)=R^q\Gamma(U,-)(M)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $\Gamma(U,-):\Mod(\mathcal O)\to\mathbf{Ab}$ the additive left exact evaluation functor $N\mapsto N(U)$; these right derived functors are computed by injective resolutions in module sheaves, not by assuming the underlying abelian sheaf of an injective module sheaf is injective.

proof.text: Let $\mathrm{Cov}$ consist of all finite basis coverings. The refinement hypothesis says precisely that, for each $U\in\mathcal B$, these coverings are cofinal among coverings of $U$: each member of the refinement maps over $U$ to a member of the original covering. Closure under fibre products puts every object occurring in their Cech complexes in $\mathcal B$. Use the chosen products, alternating restrictions and ordered tuples of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. No coproduct object $\coprod_a V_a$ in the site is needed. In Lean the finite family is indexed in the common universe by ULift (Fin m); private reindexCech, unliftExact and liftExact transport positive exactness in both directions by precomposing cochains with ULift.up or ULift.down. Their alternating differentials commute term by term.

If $I$ is an injective module sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-injective-presheaf] makes its underlying module presheaf injective. For every finite basis covering and every $p>0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-injective-presheaf-module-cech-cocycle-lift] with $q=p-1$: a closed degree-$p$ cochain $c$ is $\delta b$ for a degree-$(p-1)$ cochain $b$. Thus every positive cocycle is a boundary, proving the first assertion. The common universe convention ensures that the free module presheaves required by this cited lifting theorem belong to the very presheaf category in which $I$ is injective; a finite index set lies in that universe.

Let $A$ be any module sheaf whose positive Cech cohomology vanishes for every member of $\mathrm{Cov}$. The category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Choose a monomorphism $A\to I$ with $I$ injective and its cokernel $Q$, giving $0\to A\to I\to Q\to0$ in module sheaves. This also gives a short exact sequence of underlying abelian sheaves: kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and its cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient; [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] specifies that module sheafification is the abelian sheafification equipped with the extended module action. Consequently the underlying cokernel and kernel are exactly the abelian ones, without asserting that $I_{ab}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 03F9, proof, injective embedding and quotient; module embedding: Injectives Tag 01DU (theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives)

proof.text: For each $U\in\mathcal B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-ses-cech-h1-surjective] to this short exact sequence of underlying abelian sheaves and the cofinal set of finite basis coverings of $U$. Its degree-one vanishing hypothesis holds for $A$, so $I(U)\to Q(U)$ is surjective. Explicitly, locally lift $s\in Q(U)$ to sections $i_a\in I(V_a)$ on such a finite refinement. On overlaps $i_b-i_a$ is the image of a unique section $c_{ab}$ of $A$, and $c_{bc}-c_{ac}+c_{ab}=0$ on triple products by cancellation and the injectivity of $A\to I$ on sections. Vanishing of $\check H^1$ gives $c_{ab}=b_b-b_a$. Replacing $i_a$ by $i_a-b_a$ makes the lifts agree on overlaps; they glue in $I$ to a preimage of $s$. Left exactness on sections follows from the sectionwise kernel description, so $0\to A(U)\to I(U)\to Q(U)\to0$ is short exact for every basis object. For the cited theorem, Cov consists of coverings whose index type is ULift (Fin m), with every member in B. Presieve.ofArrows_comp_eq_of_surjective proves that lifting or lowering this index does not change the covering presieve. The exact functor SheafOfModules.toSheaf sends the module short exact sequence to the abelian sheaf sequence used here.

source.place: Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof; Tag 03F9, proof, surjectivity on the collection

proof.text: For each $\mathcal V\in\mathrm{Cov}$ all its iterated intersections are in $\mathcal B$ by step 1. Taking in degree $p$ the finite product of the section sequences of step 4 gives a short exact sequence of Cech cochain groups: kernels are coordinatewise, and a tuple in the quotient has a preimage obtained by choosing a preimage in each of its finitely many coordinates. The maps commute with alternating restrictions by naturality. Hence $0\to\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,A)\to\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,I)\to\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,Q)\to0$ is degreewise short exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], for $p>0$ the sequence $\check H^p(\mathcal V,I)\to\check H^p(\mathcal V,Q)\to\check H^{p+1}(\mathcal V,A)$ is exact. Both outside groups vanish, the first by step 2 and the last by the hypothesis on $A$. Thus $Q$ has the same positive Cech vanishing property as $A$. Use the products hypothesis on the ULift-indexed covering and reindex back to Fin m. Its degreewise short exactness follows by choosing preimages in each coordinate and sectionwise kernel exactness. SiteCechComplex.comparison_exists transports the vanishing from these chosen products to the arbitrary products S in the conclusion.

proof.text: Apply the existing generic dimension-shifting criterion [lem-pc-right-acyclic-of-epi-map-g] to the additive left exact evaluation functor in module sheaves and the property P of positive Cech vanishing on all finite basis coverings. Step 2 supplies P for injectives, step 5 supplies closure under cokernels in short exact sequences whose first two terms satisfy P, and step 4 gives epimorphic evaluation of quotient maps when the first term satisfies P. The criterion embeds A into an injective, takes its cokernel Q in P, uses the degree-zero surjectivity for degree one, and inducts on the degree with the derived long exact sequence. Enough injectives follows from the Grothendieck theorem of step 3. Finally InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj identifies the resulting zero derived evaluation with the homology of the evaluation of any specified injective resolution, exactly as required by the conclusion.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site with finite fibre products, and for an object
$U$ write $\mathbb Z[U]$ for the free abelian sheaf on $U$, so that
$H^q(U,F)=\operatorname{Ext}^q(\mathbb Z[U],F)$ for an abelian sheaf $F$.

1. If $f\colon V\to U$ generates a covering sieve, the augmented Cech complex
   $$
   \cdots\to\mathbb Z[V\times_UV\times_UV]\to\mathbb Z[V\times_UV]\to
   \mathbb Z[V]\to\mathbb Z[U]\to0
   $$
   of free abelian sheaves, with alternating-face differentials, is exact.
   Consequently, for an injective abelian sheaf $I$ the Cech complex
   [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] of $I$ along $f$ has no positive cohomology.
2. *(Cartan's criterion.)* Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf and $P$ a class of
   objects of $\mathcal C$. Suppose that for every $P$-object $U$ and every
   covering sieve $R$ of $U$ there is $f\colon V\to U$ such that: $f$ generates
   a covering sieve; every term $V\times_U\cdots\times_UV$ of its Cech nerve is
   a $P$-object; every positive-degree Cech cocycle of $F$ along $f$ is a
   coboundary; and every class in $H^{q}(U,F)$, $q>0$, whose restrictions to
   all members of $R$ vanish, also vanishes after restriction along $f$. Then
   $H^q(U,F)=0$ for every $P$-object $U$ and every $q>0$.

proof.text:
*(1).* Exactness is a local assertion. Locally on a test object $T\to U$, the
sieve generated by $f$ is covering, so after passing to a covering of $T$ the
map $T\to U$ lifts to $V$. Inserting that lift as first coordinate defines a
contracting homotopy $h$ of the augmented complex of free abelian presheaves
evaluated at $T$: the alternating-face differential satisfies
$\partial h+h\partial=1$, since adjacent inserted faces cancel. A local chain
has finite support, so one common covering suffices for all its generators;
the same construction in degree zero shows that $\mathbb Z[V]\to\mathbb Z[U]$
is an epimorphism. Sheafification is exact, so the complex of free abelian
sheaves is exact. By the free-sheaf adjunction
$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z[W],I)=I(W)$, applying
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ gives the augmented Cech complex of
[def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] along $f$, which is exact because $I$ is injective.

*(2).* We prove by strong induction on $p\geq0$ that every
$\xi\in H^{p+1}(U,F)=\operatorname{Ext}^{p+1}(\mathbb Z[U],F)$ vanishes, for all
$P$-objects $U$. A positive-degree class vanishes locally: there is a covering
sieve $R$ of $U$ on whose members $\xi$ restricts to zero (realize $\xi$ by an
injective resolution; a cocycle is locally a coboundary). Choose $f\colon V\to
U$ as in the hypothesis; then $\xi$ restricts to zero along $f$. By (1) the
complex $\mathbb Z[V_\bullet]$ of the Cech nerve is a resolution of
$\mathbb Z[U]$. The dimension-shifting lemma for $\operatorname{Ext}$ along a
resolution shows that $\xi=0$ provided $\xi$ restricts to zero along the
augmentation, every positive-degree Cech cocycle of $F$ along $f$ is a
coboundary, and $\operatorname{Ext}^{q}(\mathbb Z[V_n],F)=0$ for $0<q\leq p$.
The first two conditions hold by the choice of $f$, and the third by the
induction hypothesis, since every $V_n$ is a $P$-object. This is Cartan's
criterion, compare [Stacks Project, Tag 03F9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03F9).
